messages:
customer_jane: hitting intermittent timeouts when streaming long completions (20-30s). starts streaming tokens then drops with a socket timeout. happened after I set a global timeout in env, wondering if I mis-configured something
amy_support: sorry about that — can you paste the minimal repro and your SDK version + how you set timeouts?
customer_jane: repro below. using redwood-python 0.9.1 from pip. I set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=30000 in our CI env and call client like:
```py
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=... , timeout=30)  # I thought this is seconds
resp = client.chat.stream(model='gpt-lite', messages=[{...}])
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```
logs:
```
stream read error: timed out after 30s
socket.timeout: timed out
```
customer_jane: interestingly if I remove the env var it runs longer but still sometimes cuts at ~15s
amy_support: thanks. couple quick checks: 1) pip show redwood-sdk or pip show redwood to confirm package; 2) are you using streaming iterator or reading .text property? 3) any proxies/load balancers?
customer_jane: pip show redwood-sdk returns 0.9.1, proxy=no. I use iterator (for chunk in resp).
ryan_eng: quick heads-up — we had a known bug in 0.9.x where the client interpreted client timeout param as seconds but REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS env var was applied as milliseconds to a different socket deadline. that could create "deadline collisions" where the chunk-read socket deadline is shorter. also older streaming code applied the total request deadline incorrectly which caused premature EOF on long generations.
customer_jane: ah that would explain the weird 15s cutoffs. what should I do?
amy_support: two immediate options: upgrade to 1.2.0 where this was fixed, or explicitly set both env var and client args consistently (both in seconds or both in ms) as a temporary workaround. also set read_timeout or stream_chunk_timeout if available.
ryan_eng: repro hints: run this quick inspector to see effective config:
```sh
python -c "import redwood_sdk as r; print(r.__version__); print(r.config.get('timeout'), r.config.get('timeout_ms'), r.config.get('stream_chunk_timeout'))"
```
chris_oncall: server-side trace (from our logs around your request IDs) shows client-side cancel at ~15s, and gateway applied default chunk deadline 15000ms because the env var was parsed as int and truncated in 0.9.1. that matches the symptoms.
support-bot: Ticket #54281 auto-escalated to eng-runtime due to repeated streaming timeouts :ticket:
amy_support: if you can upgrade, try: `pip install --upgrade redwood-sdk==1.2.0` then test. If you can't upgrade immediately, set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 and pass timeout=60 in client (explicit seconds) to keep them aligned. also as workaround set `stream_chunk_timeout=60000` in client config if available.
customer_jane: upgrading to 1.2.0 locally now, will report back. thanks for the quick diagnosis.
(customer_jane later): upgraded -> 1.2.0, ran same test, long streaming completes reliably now, no socket.timeout seen. thanks!
amy_support: awesome — marking this resolved for now. we'll follow up to see if we should backport a hotfix for any other 0.9.x users.
ryan_eng: filed follow-up internal bug: INF-1289 (timeout env vs client arg parsing mismatch). notes include repro, log snippets, and suggested doc clarification to show units for each config option.
chris_oncall: if you see any more weird cutoffs, please include request id and attach full debug logs (set REDWOOD_DEBUG=1)
customer_jane: will do, thanks all :raised_hands:
